sanskrit: tatas tūryasahasrāṇi bherīṇām ayutāni ca vādyamānāny arocanta meghaśabdā yathā divi
english: Then thousands of trumpets and tens of thousands of kettledrums, being sounded, rang out splendidly, like the voices of the storm-clouds in the sky.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tad vākyaṃ rathastho rathasattamaḥ abhyabhāṣata rādheyaḥ śalyaṃ yuddhaviśāradam
english: Receiving that speech, Rādheya, best of chariot-warriors, standing upon his car, addressed Śalya, who was skilled in war:

sanskrit: codayāśvān mahābāho yāvad dhanmi dhanaṃjayam bhīmasenaṃ yamau cobhau rājānaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: "Urge on the horses, O mighty-armed one, that I may slay Dhanaṃjaya, Bhīmasena, both twins, and King Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: adya paśyatu me śalya bāhuvīryaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ asyataḥ kaṅkapatrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
english: "Today, O Śalya, let Dhanaṃjaya behold the strength of my arms, as I loose thousands and hundreds of heron-feathered shafts."

sanskrit: adya kṣepsyāmy ahaṃ śalya śarān paramatejanān pāṇḍavānāṃ vināśāya duryodhanajayāya ca
english: "Today, O Śalya, I will hurl arrows of surpassing keenness, for the destruction of the Pāṇḍavas and for Duryodhana's victory."

sanskrit: śalya uvāca sūtaputra kathaṃ nu tvaṃ pāṇḍavān avamanyase sarvāstrajñān maheṣvāsān sarvān eva mahārathān
english: Śalya said: O son of a charioteer, how is it that you make light of the Pāṇḍavas, who are masters of every weapon, mighty archers, and all of them great chariot-warriors?

sanskrit: anivartino mahābhāgān ajeyān satyavikramān api saṃjanayeyur ye bhayaṃ sākṣāc chatakratoḥ
english: Men who never turn back, exalted, unconquerable, true in valor — who could strike fear into the very Lord of a Hundred Sacrifices himself.

sanskrit: yadā śroṣyasi nirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ rādheya gāṇḍivasyājau tadā naivaṃ vadiṣyasi
english: When you hear the roar of the Gāṇḍīva in battle, O Rādheya, like the crashing of the thunderbolt, then you will speak no more like this.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca anādṛtya tu tad vākyaṃ madrarājena bhāṣitam drakṣyasy adyety avocad vai śalyaṃ karṇo nareśvara
english: Saṃjaya said: But disregarding that speech uttered by the king of the Madras, Karṇa said to Śalya, "You shall see today," O lord of men.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ yuyutsuṃ samavasthitam cukruśuḥ kuravaḥ sarve hṛṣṭarūpāḥ paraṃtapa
english: Seeing Karṇa, the mighty archer, stationed and eager for battle, all the Kurus, their faces glad, raised a shout, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tato dundubhighoṣeṇa bherīṇāṃ ninadena ca bāṇaśabdaiś ca vividhair garjitaiś ca tarasvinām niryayus tāvakā yuddhe mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: Then, amid the thunder of drums and the din of kettledrums, the varied twang of arrows, and the roars of the swift warriors, your men went forth to battle, having made death their only turning-back.

sanskrit: prayāte tu tataḥ karṇe yodheṣu muditeṣu ca cacāla pṛthivī rājan rarāsa ca suvisvaram
english: As Karṇa set forth and the warriors rejoiced, the earth trembled, O king, and gave forth a loud, shrill cry.

sanskrit: niścaranto vyadṛśyanta sūryāt sapta mahāgrahāḥ ulkāpātaś ca saṃjajñe diśāṃ dāhas tathaiva ca tathāśanyaś ca saṃpetur vavur vātāś ca dāruṇāḥ
english: Seven great planets were seen issuing forth from the sun; a falling of meteors occurred, and a burning of the quarters of the sky; thunderbolts crashed down, and dreadful winds blew.

sanskrit: mṛgapakṣigaṇāś caiva bahuśaḥ pṛtanāṃ tava apasavyaṃ tadā cakrur vedayanto mahad bhayam
english: And flocks of beasts and birds, many in number, then circled your army from the left, foretelling a great terror.

sanskrit: prasthitasya ca karṇasya nipetus turagā bhuvi asthivarṣaṃ ca patitam antarikṣād bhayānakam
english: As Karṇa set out, his horses stumbled to the ground, and a dreadful rain of bones fell from the sky.

sanskrit: jajvaluś caiva śastrāṇi dhvajāś caiva cakampire aśrūṇi ca vyamuñcanta vāhanāni viśāṃ pate
english: The weapons blazed, the banners shook, and the draught-animals shed tears, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahava utpātās tatra māriṣa samutpetur vināśāya kauravāṇāṃ sudāruṇāḥ
english: These and many other most dreadful portents arose there, O honored one, for the destruction of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: na ca tān gaṇayām āsuḥ sarve te daivamohitāḥ prasthitaṃ sūtaputraṃ ca jayety ūcur narā bhuvi nirjitān pāṇḍavāṃś caiva menire tava kauravāḥ
english: Yet they reckoned them as nothing, all of them deluded by fate; and as the son of the charioteer set out, the men cried, "Victory!" upon the earth, and your Kauravas deemed the Pāṇḍavas already vanquished.

sanskrit: tato rathasthaḥ paravīrahantā; bhīṣmadroṇāv āttavīryau nirīkṣya samajvalad bhārata pāvakābho; vaikartano 'sau rathakuñjaro vṛṣaḥ
english: Then that slayer of hostile heroes, standing upon his car, gazing upon Bhīṣma and Droṇa whose valor had been spent, blazed up, O Bhārata, radiant as fire — that Vaikartana, the bull among chariot-warriors, the elephant of the car.

sanskrit: sa śalyam ābhāṣya jagāda vākyaṃ; pārthasya karmāpratimaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā mānena darpeṇa ca dahyamānaḥ; krodhena dīpyann iva niḥśvasitvā
english: Addressing Śalya, he spoke these words, having beheld the matchless deeds of Pārtha; burning with pride and arrogance, blazing as if with wrath, he sighed and said:

sanskrit: nāhaṃ mahendrād api vajrapāṇeḥ; kruddhād bibhemy āttadhanū rathasthaḥ dṛṣṭvā tu bhīṣmapramukhāñ śayānān; na tv eva māṃ sthiratā saṃjahāti
english: "Bow in hand, standing on my car, I do not fear even great Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, in his wrath; yet, beholding Bhīṣma and the foremost ones laid low, my steadfastness still does not forsake me."

sanskrit: mahendraviṣṇupratimāv aninditau; rathāśvanāgapravarapramāthinau avadhyakalpau nihatau yadā parais; tato mamādyāpi raṇe 'sti sādhvasam
english: "When those two, blameless and like unto great Indra and Viṣṇu, crushers of the best of chariots, horses, and elephants, all but invincible, were slain by the foe — even now, for that, there is a trembling in me in battle."

sanskrit: samīkṣya saṃkhye 'tibalān narādhipair; narāśvamātaṅgarathāñ śarair hatān kathaṃ na sarvān ahitān raṇe 'vadhīn; mahāstravid brāhmaṇapuṃgavo guruḥ
english: "Looking upon the mighty ranks in battle — men, horses, elephants, and chariots slain by the kings' shafts — how is it that the preceptor, that bull among Brāhmaṇas, knower of the great weapons, did not slay all his enemies in the fight?"

sanskrit: sa saṃsmaran droṇahavaṃ mahāhave; bravīmi satyaṃ kuravo nibodhata na vo mad anyaḥ prasahed raṇe 'rjunaṃ; kramāgataṃ mṛtyum ivograrūpiṇam
english: "Recalling the slaying of Droṇa in the great combat, I speak the truth — mark it, O Kurus: none other than I among you could withstand Arjuna in battle, when he comes on like death itself in fearful form."

sanskrit: śikṣā prasādaś ca balaṃ dhṛtiś ca; droṇe mahāstrāṇi ca saṃnatiś ca sa ced agān mṛtyuvaśaṃ mahātmā; sarvān anyān āturān adya manye
english: "Training, graciousness, strength, and firmness, the great weapons and humility were in Droṇa; if that great soul has gone into the power of death, then I deem all the rest stricken helpless today."

sanskrit: neha dhruvaṃ kiṃ cid api pracintyaṃ; vidur loke karmaṇo 'nityayogāt sūryodaye ko hi vimuktasaṃśayo; garvaṃ kurvītādya gurau nipātite
english: "Nothing here, they know, is to be reckoned as certain in this world, because of the impermanence of action's fruit. At sunrise, who, freed of doubt, would take pride today, when the preceptor has been struck down?"

sanskrit: na nūnam astrāṇi balaṃ parākramaḥ; kriyā sunītaṃ paramāyudhāni vā alaṃ manuṣyasya sukhāya vartituṃ; tathā hi yuddhe nihataḥ parair guruḥ
english: "Surely neither weapons, nor strength, nor prowess, nor skill, nor sound policy, nor the supreme arms suffice to keep a man in happiness — for so the preceptor was slain in battle by the foe."

sanskrit: hutāśanādityasamānatejasaṃ; parākrame viṣṇupuraṃdaropamam naye bṛhaspatyuśanaḥsamaṃ sadā; na cainam astraṃ tad apāt suduḥsaham
english: "Him whose splendor equaled fire and the sun, who in prowess was like Viṣṇu and Purandara, ever in counsel the peer of Bṛhaspati and Uśanas — even him that hard-to-bear weaponry could not save."

sanskrit: saṃprakruṣṭe ruditastrīkumāre; parābhūte pauruṣe dhārtarāṣṭre mayā kṛtyam iti jānāmi śalya; prayāhi tasmād dviṣatām anīkam
english: "With outcry raised, women and children weeping, the manhood of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's host brought low — I know what must be done by me, O Śalya: therefore advance against the army of our enemies."

sanskrit: yatra rājā pāṇḍavaḥ satyasaṃdho; vyavasthito bhīmasenārjunau ca vāsudevaḥ sṛñjayāḥ sātyakiś ca; yamau ca kas tau viṣahen mad anyaḥ
english: "There, where the Pāṇḍava king, true to his word, stands firm, with Bhīmasena and Arjuna, Vāsudeva, the Sṛñjayas, Sātyaki, and the twins — who but I could endure those two?"

sanskrit: tasmāt kṣipraṃ madrapate prayāhi; raṇe pāñcālān pāṇḍavān sṛñjayāṃś ca tān vā haniṣyāmi sametya saṃkhye; yāsyāmi vā droṇamukhāya manye
english: "Therefore advance swiftly, O lord of the Madras, against the Pāñcālas, the Pāṇḍavas, and the Sṛñjayas in battle. Either I shall slay them, joining combat, or I think I shall go the way of Droṇa."

sanskrit: na tv evāhaṃ na gamiṣyāmi madhyaṃ; teṣāṃ śūrāṇām iti mā śalya viddhi mitradroho marṣaṇīyo na me 'yaṃ; tyaktvā prāṇān anuyāsyāmi droṇam
english: "But know me thus, O Śalya: it is not that I will not go into the midst of those heroes. Treachery toward a friend is not to be borne by me; giving up my life, I will follow after Droṇa."

sanskrit: prājñasya mūḍhasya ca jīvitānte; prāṇapramokṣo 'ntakavaktragasya ato vidvann abhiyāsyāmi pārthaṃ; diṣṭaṃ na śakyaṃ vyativartituṃ vai
english: "For wise man and fool alike, at life's end, the release of breath comes to him who has reached the jaws of the Ender. Therefore, O learned one, I will go forth against Pārtha; what is ordained cannot be overstepped."

sanskrit: kalyāṇavṛttaḥ satataṃ hi rājan; vaicitravīryasya suto mamāsīt tasyārthasiddhyartham ahaṃ tyajāmi; priyān bhogān dustyajaṃ jīvitaṃ ca
english: "For ever of gracious conduct toward me, O king, has the son of Vicitravīrya been; for the achievement of his purpose I give up dear pleasures and life that is so hard to surrender."

sanskrit: vaiyāghracarmāṇam akūjanākṣaṃ; haimatrikośaṃ rajatatriveṇum rathaprabarhaṃ turagaprabarhair; yuktaṃ prādān mahyam idaṃ hi rāmaḥ
english: "Decked with tiger-skin, its axle never creaking, with a triple golden scabbard and a silver triple yoke-pole — this best of chariots, yoked with the finest steeds, Rāma gave to me."

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi citrāṇi nirīkṣya śalya; dhvajaṃ gadāṃ sāyakāṃś cograrūpān asiṃ ca dīptaṃ paramāyudhaṃ ca; śaṅkhaṃ ca śubhraṃ svanavantam ugram
english: "Behold, O Śalya, the splendid bows, the banner, the mace, the arrows of fearful form, the blazing sword, the supreme weapon, and the bright conch, loud-resounding and terrible."

sanskrit: patākinaṃ vajranipātanisvanaṃ; sitāśvayuktaṃ śubhatūṇaśobhitam imaṃ samāsthāya rathaṃ ratharṣabhaṃ; raṇe haniṣyāmy aham arjunaṃ balāt
english: "Mounting this bull among chariots — pennoned, roaring like the falling thunderbolt, yoked with white horses, adorned with fair quivers — I shall slay Arjuna in battle by main force."

sanskrit: taṃ cen mṛtyuḥ sarvaharo 'bhirakṣate; sadāpramattaḥ samare pāṇḍuputram taṃ vā haniṣyāmi sametya yuddhe; yāsyāmi vā bhīṣmamukho yamāya
english: "If death, the taker of all, ever-vigilant, guards that son of Pāṇḍu in battle, then either I shall slay him, joining combat, or I shall go to Yama by the road that Bhīṣma went."

sanskrit: yamavaruṇakuberavāsavā vā; yadi yugapat sagaṇā mahāhave jugupiṣava ihaitya pāṇḍavaṃ; kim u bahunā saha tair jayāmi tam
english: "Even if Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Vāsava, with their hosts, were to come all at once into the great battle to guard the Pāṇḍava — what need of many words? — I would conquer him together with them."

sanskrit: iti raṇarabhasasya katthatas; tad upaniśamya vacaḥ sa madrarāṭ avahasad avamanya vīryavān; pratiṣiṣidhe ca jagāda cottaram
english: Hearing the words of one thus boasting in the frenzy of battle, that valiant king of the Madras laughed in scorn, rebuked him, and made reply:

sanskrit: virama virama karṇa katthanād; atirabhaso 'syati cāpy ayuktavāk kva ca hi naravaro dhanaṃjayaḥ; kva punar iha tvam upāramābudha
english: "Cease, cease, O Karṇa, from your boasting; you are too rash, and your speech is unfitting. Where is Dhanaṃjaya, that best of men, and where, then, are you? Have done, O foolish one!"

sanskrit: yadusadanam upendrapālitaṃ; tridivam ivāmararājarakṣitam prasabham iha vilokya ko haret; puruṣavarāvarajām ṛte 'rjunāt
english: "The dwelling of the Yadus, guarded by Upendra like heaven warded by the king of the gods — who, beholding it, could carry off by force the younger sister of that best of men, save Arjuna?"

sanskrit: tribhuvanasṛjam īśvareśvaraṃ; ka iha pumān bhavam āhvayed yudhi mṛgavadhakalahe ṛte 'rjunāt; surapativīryasamaprabhāvataḥ
english: "Who among men here could challenge to combat Bhava, the maker of the three worlds, the Lord of lords, in a quarrel over the slaying of a deer, save Arjuna, whose might equaled the valor of the king of the gods?"

sanskrit: asurasuramahoragān narān; garuḍapiśācasayakṣarākṣasān iṣubhir ajayad agnigauravāt; svabhilaṣitaṃ ca havir dadau jayaḥ
english: "Asuras, gods, great serpents, and men, Garuḍas, piśācas, with yakṣas and rākṣasas, he conquered with his arrows out of reverence for Agni, and the victorious one gave him the oblation he desired."

sanskrit: smarasi nanu yadā parair hṛtaḥ; sa ca dhṛtarāṣṭrasuto vimokṣitaḥ dinakaraja narottamair yadā; maruṣu bahūn vinihatya tān arīn
english: "Surely you remember, O son of the sun, when that son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra was carried off by his foes and then set free by those best of men, who in the wilds slew many of those enemies?"

sanskrit: prathamam api palāyite tvayi; priyakalahā dhṛtarāṣṭrasūnavaḥ smarasi nanu yadā pramocitāḥ; khacaragaṇān avajitya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: "When you had fled at the very first, the strife-loving sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — surely you remember when they were rescued by the Pāṇḍavas, who overcame the hosts of the sky-rangers?"

sanskrit: samuditabalavāhanāḥ punaḥ; puruṣavareṇa jitāḥ stha gograhe sagurugurusutāḥ sabhīṣmakāḥ; kim u na jitaḥ sa tadā tvayārjunaḥ
english: "Again, at the seizing of the cattle, you all — with your full strength and steeds, together with the preceptor and his son and Bhīṣma — were vanquished by that best of men. Was not Arjuna unconquered by you then as well?"

sanskrit: idam aparam upasthitaṃ punas; tava nidhanāya suyuddham adya vai yadi na ripubhayāt palāyase; samaragato 'dya hato 'si sūtaja
english: "Now this further fine battle has come upon you again, this very day, for your destruction. If you do not flee out of fear of the foe, then, gone to war this day, you are as good as slain, O son of a charioteer."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca iti bahuparuṣaṃ prabhāṣati; pramanasi madrapatau ripustavam bhṛśam atiruṣitaḥ paraṃ vṛṣaḥ; kurupṛtanāpatir āha madrapam
english: Saṃjaya said: As the lord of the Madras, with cheerful mind, was thus speaking many harsh words in praise of the foe, that mighty bull, the commander of the Kuru host, exceedingly enraged, said to the king of the Madras:

sanskrit: bhavatu bhavatu kiṃ vikatthase; nanu mama tasya ca yuddham udyatam yadi sa jayati māṃ mahāhave; tata idam astu sukatthitaṃ tava
english: "So be it, so be it — why do you boast? Surely the battle between me and him is at hand. If he conquers me in the great combat, then let this fair boasting of yours stand proven."

sanskrit: evam astv iti madreśa uktvā nottaram uktavān yāhi madreśa cāpy enaṃ karṇaḥ prāha yuyutsayā
english: "So be it," said the lord of the Madras, and made no further reply. "Drive on, O lord of the Madras," Karṇa then said to him, eager for battle.

sanskrit: sa rathaḥ prayayau śatrūñ śvetāśvaḥ śalyasārathiḥ nighnann amitrān samare tamo ghnan savitā yathā
english: That chariot, with white horses and Śalya for its driver, advanced upon the enemies, smiting foes in battle as the sun dispels the darkness.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyāt prītimān vai rathena; vaiyāghreṇa śvetayujātha karṇaḥ sa cālokya dhvajinīṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ tvarayā paryapṛcchat
english: Then Karṇa, well pleased, advanced upon his car decked with tiger-skin and yoked with white steeds; and looking upon the bannered host of the Pāṇḍavas, he hastily asked after Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prayān eva tadā karṇo harṣayan vāhinīṃ tava ekaikaṃ samare dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavaṃ paryapṛcchata
english: Saṃjaya said: Even as he advanced, Karṇa, gladdening your army, kept asking after the Pāṇḍava, scanning each warrior in the battle one by one.

sanskrit: yo mamādya mahātmānaṃ darśayec chvetavāhanam tasmai dadyām abhipretaṃ varaṃ yaṃ manasecchati
english: "Whoever today shows me that great soul, the one with white steeds, to him I would grant whatever desired boon his heart wishes."

sanskrit: sa cet tad abhimanyeta tasmai dadyām ahaṃ punaḥ śakaṭaṃ ratnasaṃpūrṇaṃ yo me brūyād dhanaṃjayam
english: "And if he should think that not enough, then to him who tells me of Dhanaṃjaya I would give besides a cartload filled with jewels."

sanskrit: sa cet tad abhimanyeta puruṣo 'rjunadarśivān anyaṃ tasmai punar dadyāṃ sauvarṇaṃ hastiṣaḍgavam
english: "And if that man who has pointed out Arjuna should think that not enough, then I would give him yet another gift — a golden elephant and six oxen."

sanskrit: tathā tasmai punar dadyāṃ strīṇāṃ śatam alaṃkṛtam śyāmānāṃ niṣkakaṇṭhīnāṃ gītavādyavipaścitām
english: "And to him I would give, besides, a hundred adorned women, dark and lovely, golden chains about their throats, skilled in song and music."

sanskrit: sa cet tad abhimanyeta puruṣo 'rjunadarśivān anyaṃ tasmai varaṃ dadyāṃ śvetān pañcaśatān hayān
english: "And if that man who has shown me Arjuna should think that not enough, then I would give him another gift — five hundred white horses."

sanskrit: hemabhāṇḍaparicchannān sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalān sudāntān api caivāhaṃ dadyām aṣṭaśatān parān
english: "And I would give, moreover, eight hundred other steeds, decked with golden trappings and bright jeweled ear-ornaments, and well broken in."

sanskrit: rathaṃ ca śubhraṃ sauvarṇaṃ dadyāṃ tasmai svalaṃkṛtam yuktaṃ paramakāmbojair yo me brūyād dhanaṃjayam
english: "And to him who tells me of Dhanaṃjaya I would give a bright golden chariot, richly adorned, yoked with the finest Kāmboja steeds."

sanskrit: anyaṃ tasmai varaṃ dadyāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ śatāni ṣaṭ kāñcanair vividhair bhāṇḍair ācchannān hemamālinaḥ utpannān aparānteṣu vinītān hastiśikṣakaiḥ
english: "To him I would give another gift — six hundred elephants, covered with various golden trappings and wearing golden garlands, bred in the western lands and trained by elephant-tamers."

sanskrit: sa cet tad abhimanyeta puruṣo 'rjunadarśivān anyaṃ tasmai varaṃ dadyāṃ yam asau kāmayet svayam
english: "And if that man who has shown me Arjuna should think that not enough, then I would give him another gift — whatever he himself might desire."

sanskrit: putradārān vihārāṃś ca yad anyad vittam asti me tac ca tasmai punar dadyāṃ yad yat sa manasecchati
english: "My sons and wives, my pleasure-houses, and whatever other wealth is mine — that too I would give him, whatever his heart should wish."

sanskrit: hatvā ca sahitau kṛṣṇau tayor vittāni sarvaśaḥ tasmai dadyām ahaṃ yo me prabrūyāt keśavārjunau
english: "And having slain the two Kṛṣṇas together, I would give all their wealth entirely to him who tells me of Keśava and Arjuna."

sanskrit: etā vācaḥ subahuśaḥ karṇa uccārayan yudhi dadhmau sāgarasaṃbhūtaṃ susvanaṃ śaṅkham uttamam
english: Uttering these words again and again in the battle, Karṇa blew his excellent, sweet-sounding conch, born of the sea.

sanskrit: tā vācaḥ sūtaputrasya tathā yuktā niśamya tu duryodhano mahārāja prahṛṣṭaḥ sānugo 'bhavat
english: Hearing those well-spoken words of the son of the charioteer, Duryodhana, O great king, was delighted, together with his followers.

sanskrit: tato dundubhinirghoṣo mṛdaṅgānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ siṃhanādaḥ savāditraḥ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca nisvanaḥ
english: Then the thunder of drums and tabors on every side, the lion-roar mingled with instruments, and the trumpeting of elephants —

sanskrit: prādurāsīt tadā rājaṃs tvatsainye bharatarṣabha yodhānāṃ saṃprahṛṣṭānāṃ tathā samabhavat svanaḥ
english: — arose then, O king, in your army, O bull of the Bharatas; and such was the clamor of the warriors in their high joy.

sanskrit: tathā prahṛṣṭe sainye tu plavamānaṃ mahāratham vikatthamānaṃ samare rādheyam arikarśanam madrarājaḥ prahasyedaṃ vacanaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: And while the army thus rejoiced, the king of the Madras, with a laugh, addressed these words in reply to Rādheya, that tormentor of foes, who, sweeping along on his great chariot, was boasting in the midst of battle:

sanskrit: mā sūtaputra mānena sauvarṇaṃ hastiṣaḍgavam prayaccha puruṣāyādya drakṣyasi tvaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: "Do not, O son of a charioteer, out of pride bestow the golden elephant and the six oxen upon any man today: you shall see Dhanaṃjaya for yourself."

sanskrit: bālyād iva tvaṃ tyajasi vasu vaiśravaṇo yathā ayatnenaiva rādheya draṣṭāsy adya dhanaṃjayam
english: "As if from childishness you fling away your wealth like Vaiśravaṇa; without any effort at all, O Rādheya, you shall behold Dhanaṃjaya today."

sanskrit: parāsṛjasi mithyā kiṃ kiṃ ca tvaṃ bahu mūḍhavat apātradāne ye doṣās tān mohān nāvabudhyase
english: "Why do you squander all this in vain, and why, like a fool, do you talk so much? The faults that lie in giving to the unworthy — those, in your delusion, you do not perceive."

sanskrit: yat pravedayase vittaṃ bahutvena khalu tvayā śakyaṃ bahuvidhair yajñair yaṣṭuṃ sūta yajasva taiḥ
english: "With the wealth you proclaim, abundant indeed, you could perform many kinds of sacrifices; offer them up in worship, O charioteer's son."

sanskrit: yac ca prārthayase hantuṃ kṛṣṇau mohān mṛṣaiva tat na hi śuśruma saṃmarde kroṣṭrā siṃhau nipātitau
english: "And that you seek to slay the two Kṛṣṇas — that, from delusion, is mere idle fancy; for we have never heard of two lions struck down in the fray by a jackal."

sanskrit: aprārthitaṃ prārthayase suhṛdo na hi santi te ye tvāṃ na vārayanty āśu prapatantaṃ hutāśane
english: "You crave what is not to be craved; you have no true friends, since they do not at once restrain you as you fall headlong into the fire."

sanskrit: kālakāryaṃ na jānīṣe kālapakvo 'sy asaṃśayam bahvabaddham akarṇīyaṃ ko hi brūyāj jijīviṣuḥ
english: "You do not know what the hour requires; you are ripened by Time, beyond doubt. Who that wished to live would utter such rambling, unfitting nonsense?"

sanskrit: samudrataraṇaṃ dorbhyāṃ kaṇṭhe baddhvā yathā śilām giryagrād vā nipatanaṃ tādṛk tava cikīrṣitam
english: "Like crossing the ocean with your two arms after binding a stone about your neck, or like leaping down from a mountain-peak — such is the thing you mean to do."

sanskrit: sahitaḥ sarvayodhais tvaṃ vyūḍhānīkaiḥ surakṣitaḥ dhanaṃjayena yudhyasva śreyaś cet prāptum icchasi
english: "Joined with all your warriors, well guarded by arrayed troops, do battle with Dhanaṃjaya, if you wish to attain what is best."

sanskrit: hitārthaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya bravīmi tvā na hiṃsayā śraddhatsvaitan mayā proktaṃ yadi te 'sti jijīviṣā
english: "For the good of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son I speak to you, not out of malice. Believe this that I have told you, if there is in you any wish to live."
